From the results, we can infer that the Decision Tree Classifier performs the best in terms of classification and in clustering algorithms produced on the dataset, the AdaBoost algorithm performs better compared to the K-Means algorithm. While in Ensemble methods, a combination of Decision tree and Logistic regression exhibits higher performance Finally, this paper substructures the expediency of using machine learning algorithms to estimate the energy performance of buildings as a beneficial and authentic approach.

articleTitle: A Near Optimal Smart Door Security System Based on Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: This project aims to solve the security problem faced by digital door locking system. By integrating technologies such as computer vision, image processing, internet of things and deep learning various solutions can be developed for a digital to locking system. Most of the existing system fails to recognize the person who wears a mask aur covered in mud etc. This was due to minimum accuracy and reliability. In this regard the proposed approach uses deep learning method to recognize a face using mask or mud. The proposed approach also comes with a cost effective iot based system using principal component analysis. Modifications have been done in Eigen face algorithm which is used by proposed approach. This algorithm is used in the case of component images which are blurred and get clear face recognition automatically. During the comparison it has been identified that proposed approach performs well then the existing approaches.

articleTitle: Virtual Handwriting Based Smart Board Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Writing is a specific technique for communication that allows us to express our ideas. The two most common methods for recording information are typing and writing. The process involves using a pen or a finger to inscribe letters or words in a relaxed environment. With wearable devices capable of observing and comprehending our actions, gesture recognitionhas become a computational technique that strives to identify and comprehend human gestures using mathematical algorithms. Our project aims to exploit this technology to develop a motion- to-text converter, a software program for smart wearable devices designed for writing in the air. The application will utilize computer vision to track finger movement, with the resulting text having diverse applications, including text messaging and emailing. This technology will prove beneficial in facilitating communication for people with hearing impairments.

articleTitle: Transfer Learning-Based Method for Classifying Yoga Poses Using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Yoga is a popular practice that aims to improve one's health and well-being through physical postures, breathing exercises, and meditation. The growing popularity of yoga has prompted researchers to focus on automating the process of classifying yoga poses. Using deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transfer learning, we present a deep learning-based method for correctly categorizing yoga postures in this research. The primary goal of this study is to develop an efficient method for automatically recognizing and categorizing yoga poses in given photographs. The impressive success of deep CNNs in picture classification tasks is exploited here to accomplish this goal. We also use transfer learning, a method for customizing pre-trained CNN models for our unique yoga posture categorization task. This paper presents a Transfer Learning based Method for Yoga Poses classification using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (TLMYPC-DCNN). The proposed model uses the Yoga Posture Dataset for classification of images. Initially, this model starts with pre-processing the input images by splitting input data into three groups such as training set, validation set and test data. The deep learning CNN model will be trained using the training data, and then its parameters will be tweaked using the validation data. Finally, the test data will be used to assess how well the data performs. A convolutional neural network (CNN) model called MobileNetV2 will be applied to the model photos. The experimental results show that the suggested TLMYPC-DCNN based technique with transfer learning is effective at accurately and reliably classifying yoga poses.

articleTitle: Power Quality Control Measures for Grid Connected EV with Renewable Energy Resources
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: The increasing use of Electric Vehicles in consumer and commercial markets is transforming the electricity generation and distribution infrastructure and automotive transportation infrastructure. The use of electric vehicles reduces the pollution levels to a great extent. However, a dramatic increase of Electric Vehicles and resultant imbalance in quantity of dedicated charging stations has brought forth issues pertaining to the power quality control of the charging infrastructure. The performance of grid-integrated or freestanding renewable power sources, as well as smart-grid electrical transmission networks built for Electric Vehicle charging operations, is impacted by power quality constraints. This paper discusses different optimization techniques for Electric Vehicle charging topologies and different types of energy storage systems operating in the context of the unpredictability of renewable energy sources.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Efficacy of Antivirus Software Against Malware and Rats Using Metasploit and Asyncrat
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: In the current world everyone depends on the internet for all activities such as communication, work, entertainment, shopping, financial transactions etc. This has made all the users around the world vulnerable to many cyber threats. Issues like data breaches caused a loss of around ∃4.35 million in 2022 alone. Around 236.1 million ransomware attacks occurred globally in the first half of 2022. Anti-Virus software, being the only wall of defense against these attacks, keeps upgrading themselves, but research shows that malware keeps upgrading too, thereby, avoiding detection and causing harm. So, with the help of the open-source tools like Metasploit and AsyncRAT, the paper mentions the steps to create our own malware and Random Access Trojans to detect fraudulent Anti-Virus Software in the market. To support the claims, paper also includes the steps to test the malware on different target Anti-Virus software which are deployed on different virtual machines hosted from VMWare.

articleTitle: A Survey on Eliminating Botnet and Intrusion Attacks Through Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: With the rising linkage and dependence on computer networks, the threat of intrusions and botnets has become a critical concern for organizations and those involved. Malicious actors are in control of unauthorized access or actions that harm the security and integrity of computer systems and insecure devices. The identification of attacks and botnets is of utmost importance in ensuring the security of networks and safeguarding confidential information. In recent years, there has been a growing interest among researchers and organizations in developing unique evaluation methods that can adapt to emerging threats and apply intelligent algorithms such as sparse modelling, transfer learning, distributed computing, or meta-learning capable of detecting, classifying, and predicting previously unknown attack patterns, which can result in machine learning and deep learning models that are more accurate and efficient. This review paper compares the performance of machine learning and deep learning approaches such as Naïve Bayes, Support Vector Machines (SVM), and Logical Regression for intrusion and botnet attacks in various network platforms. This paper provides a comprehensive comparison of machine-learning approaches used in the cyber realm for botnet and intrusion detection and encompasses an analysis of the datasets utilized, the specific cyber issues addressed, and the resultant outcomes. Furthermore, it offers valuable insights into the challenges and advancements within the realm of cybersecurity, thereby facilitating the development of novel approaches and technologies aimed at enhancing digital safety.

articleTitle: A Review on Exoskeleton Upper Limb Impact, Design, Selection and Application
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: This review article to provide a comprehensive overview of exoskeleton upper limb systems, including their selection criteria, applications, mechanisms, merits, demerits, suggestions for improvement, and case studies. Exoskeletons are wearable robotic devices designed to enhance human capabilities, particularly in the upper limb exoskeleton. They have gained convincing attention in last few years because of their potential to assist individuals with physical disabilities, enhance rehabilitation processes, and augment human performance in various industries. It discusses key factors such as biomechanics, ergonomics, control systems, power sources, and safety considerations. Medical rehabilitation, assistive devices for individuals with disabilities, occupational ergonomics, and industrial settings. The review highlights the potential benefits and challenges associated with each application, providing insights into the current state of research and development. These suggestions encompass areas such as user comfort, adaptability to individual needs, intuitive control interfaces, enhanced dexterity, and prolonged battery life. The practical applications of exoskeleton technology in real-world scenarios, highlighting the positive impact on users' lives. Overall, this review provides a comprehensive understanding of exoskeleton upper limb systems, their selection criteria, applications, and suggestions for improvement. By synthesizing current research and case studies, it aims to inspire further advancements in the field and promote the widespread adoption of exoskeleton technology in various domains.

articleTitle: Analysis and Implementation of Power Optimizer Using sliding Mode Control enabled String Inverter for Domestic applications
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Due to the easy accessibility of highly efficient PV panels that minimize negative environmental effects, solar photovoltaic (PV) power systems are presently used as a significant alternative power source. The household PV power plants in use are often linked together in strings or arrays before being in a grid-connected state or a load using an inverter. The research is done with the PV plant, which comprises six panels, each having a 250 Wp rating, linked in series to produce 1.5 kWp of rated power and then connected to the load through an inverter. A multiple PWM approach is employed in this system to regulate an inverter's switches. The system's main flaw is that it suffers a production loss of roughly 60% if any external elements, such a chimney or a tree, cast any shade onto one or more panels. In the proposed system, a cascaded boost converter with sliding mode control is designed to match the PV panel's source and load characteristics even while it is being shadowed by outside influences. The MATLAB/SIMULINK environment is used to model the proposed system. The system is linked to the load after the system's output from the cascaded boost converter roughly 30 V DC which is connected in series with the other five panels to create a string of 180 V DC. Using an LM318 comparator, a boost converter with sliding mode control is realized. The converter's output ranges from 28 to 30 volts. As a result, the entire system power is increased by around 30%.

articleTitle: Martian Terrain Classification through Federated Learning: A Decentralized Approach for Understanding the Mars
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: The exploration of the Martian landmass holds paramount importance in advancing spatial research as it offers valuable insights into planetary evolution and the potential for habitability beyond Earth. In this paper, a novel approach is presented to perform multi-class classification of Martian terrain into seven distinct classes, namely crater, dark dune, slope streak, bright dune, impact ejecta, swiss cheese and spider. Accurate terrain classification provides crucial insights into Martian ge-ological processes and enables informed decisions for selecting optimal landing sites for future missions. Additionally, by facili-tating the planning of safe and efficient traverses during explo-ration missions, precise terrain classification enhances the overall success and safety of these ambitious endeavors, ultimately advancing our knowledge of Mars and supporting humanity's quest for space exploration. This research harnesses the power of federated learning, an emerging decentralized machine learning paradigm, in conjunction with the DenseNet-121 architecture. This collaborative learning technique enables the model training across distributed data sources while preserving data privacy and security. Through extensive experimentation using the HiRISE dataset, obtained from the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, this research demonstrates the efficacy of the presented approach in achieving better performance and robustness. The federated DenseNet-121 model showcases promising results, laying the foundation for efficient multi-class Martian terrain classification in future spatial exploration missions and contributing to a deeper understanding of the Martian landscape.

articleTitle: A Novel Breathing Rate Estimation Framework Using 3 Distinct Types of Signals
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Breathing Rate is a vital biological characteristic that needs to be assessed in a variety of therapeutic scenarios. It is still routinely monitored in a manual fashion. Consequently, a unique methodology for estimating the BR from a PPG- Pho-toplethysmogram, ECG- electrocardiogram, or blood pressure (BP) signal is presented in this research. To extract respiration-orientated signals, the system employs DWT- Discrete Wavelet Transform as well as EMD- Empirical Mode Decomposition algorithms, utilizing both the frequency as well as time domain data. Our approach was able to obtain satisfactory efficiency even during severely distorted portions of the signals by integrating an SQI- Signal Quality Index as well as an RKF - Robust Kalman Filter. The resultant signals are merged via the fusion of the state vector, and the BR is then calculated. The methodology was evaluated on 2 general people-accessible healthcare datasets, namely, the BIDMC as well as the MIT-BIH Polysomnographic datasets. The MAPE- Mean Absolute Percentage Error was used to assess performance. The outcomes also showed that the system was resilient to noise which is almost OdB. As a result, this system may be useful for BR surveillance in raised noise environments.

articleTitle: Segmentation and Detection of Urban Objects from UAV Images Using Hybrid Deep Learning Combinations
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), commonly referred to as drones, have found numerous applications in civil disciplines such as construction inspection, infrastructure planning, precision agriculture, real-time monitoring of road traffic, and overhead power line inspection. These drones are equipped with sophisticated sensors, for example high-resolution cameras, that enable them to acquire images cost-effectively and efficiently. The images can then be processed using automated vision-based analysis and decision-making systems for easing large-scale planning and inspection purposes. One such system is the automatic detection of urban objects such as roads, buildings, trees, and manholes, from UAV images, which plays a vital role in policy planning and decision making. To achieve this objective, in this work a deep learning approach, commonly referred to semantic segmentation, and object detection are used, which involves the masking of images in a non-destructive manner, and then recognizing the various categories of objects. The above segmentation technique was attempted using two deep learning architectures namely Unet and VGG16 on the VisDrone image dataset and object detection was attempted using two algorithms namely, Rcnn and contextual learning on COCO dataset and the results were studied.

articleTitle: Time-Delayed Inertial Bidirectional Associative Memory Neural Network: A Dynamical Exploration
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: This research aims to investigate the dynamical characteristics of second-order bi-directional associative neural networks (BAM), a domain where existing literature primarily focuses on first-order neural networks. The study's primary objective is to conduct a qualitative analysis of BAM neural networks by examining the influence of time-delays. The theoretical exploration involves stability conditions and Hopf-bifurcation analysis to unveil the impact of time-delays during neuronal transmission, specifically in terms of two-neuronal BAM models. By choosing time-delay as a bifurcation parameter, the study proposes necessary and sufficient conditions using the Routh-Hurwitz stability criterion and transversality conditions. Moreover, the paper presents illustrative examples that vividly demonstrate the effects of stability and Hopf bifurcation resulting from time-delays on the dynamics of neural networks. This research contributes to a deeper understanding of the intricate behaviors of second-order BAM neural networks in the context of time-delay dynamics.

articleTitle: Comparison of Single-Phase Bidirectional AC/DC Converter for V2G Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: The two configurations of single-phase bidirectional battery chargers for vehicle-to-grid (V2G) systems are thoroughly analysed and compared in this research paper. A single-phase bidirectional AC-DC converter and a bidirectional Buck-Boost converter are featured in the first model, while a dual active bridge converter (DAB) and a single-phase bidirectional AC-DC converter are featured in the second model. This study's goal is to assess these models' performance. To maximise power transfer effectiveness, several current control methods for both models were investigated and contrasted. The effectiveness of the generated models was evaluated by comnuter simulations.

articleTitle: Advances In EEG-Based Multimodal Emotion Recognition: A Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: In the field of emotion recognition, computer-aided classification systems are typically designed to comprehend human emotional states by analyzing specific signal states. However, it is important to note that human emotional levels cannot be visualized as a single, monolithic process or event. Critical reviews in this field have consistently shown that multimodal accuracies outperform unimodal accuracies. The integration of multimodal environments adds complexity to the analysis process, which is the focus of this research. This paper presents the potential of EEG data and the integration of multimodal environments in emotion classification.

articleTitle: Prevention Strategy to Detect Reverse Shell using Security Onion in Hoax Shell
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: There are millions of virus variations, making it extremely tough to safeguard a corporation. Intrusion detection and prevention devices can identify malicious behaviour achieved by external or internal attackers by monitoring and analyzing network data. The “connect-back shell,” often referred to as a reverse shell, creates a shell session on the target system before accessing the victim's computer. The objective is to establish a connection to a remote computer and reroute the input and output connections of the target system's shell to enable remote access by the attacker. The data is delivered and displayed in the listener's system when the listener executes malicious shell code on the initiator's computer when a connection is made. The Security Onion platform includes administration options such as Secure Shell (SSH) for server and sensor management and remote web client access. The comprehensive packet capture feature of Security Onion gives the security analyst access to host, session, and network data. Security Onion's comprehensive packet capture capability gives the security analyst a wide range of monitoring, analysis, and management options by allowing access to host, session, and network data. The proposed work creates a bogus reverse shell attack that uses Security Onion to carry out the basic functions of a reverse shell and can sniff network communication between the attacker and victim.

articleTitle: Identifying Outliers, Defective Areas and Performance Evaluation of a PV Module using EL Image Processing: A Variational Autoencoder Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Enhancing the commercial viability and efficacy of PV solar cell usage necessitates a comprehensive investigation into fault identification. This study introduces the development of a defect detection system tailored for identifying solar cell defects while approximating the subsequent power and efficiency losses. The methodology proposed encompasses two primary phases: Firstly, an anomaly detection model utilizing the Variational Auto Encoder identifies defects, reconstructs defect-free solar cells or modules, and generates a heatmap illustrating defect intensities. Subsequently, in the second phase, the defective area is quantified to compute total power and efficiency losses of a PV module. The method's outcomes, utilizing Electroluminescence (EL) images, machine learning, and defect simulation, demonstrate its capability to operate with minimal available data and estimate overall power and efficiency loss. This research establishes a correlation between defects and power generation loss, offering an inclusive estimation of PV module profitability, potentially mitigating the soft costs of PV systems and enhancing fault diagnosis methods.

articleTitle: Analysis and Real-Time Implementation of Power Line Disturbances Test in Three Phase Induction Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: The main objective of the paper is to analyze and utilize the grid emulator to compare the behavior of the three-phase induction motor to voltage sags (dips). This work presents an examination of voltage sags and a short interruption immunity test of a three-phase induction motor to examine the resistance of the machine against the voltage sags and short interruptions. This happens broadly in low voltage mains. Voltage sag is an issue influencing electrical characteristics. The negative torque instigated during fault causes a reduction in speed of the machine, influences to three-stage voltage sag on the three- phase induction machine. A three-phase squirrel cage induction motor of 0.75KW/415V is tested with balancing three-phase separate voltage sag of various depths and magnitude. A similar investigation is finished regarding the waveforms of RMS current, power, and voltage sag. An investigation of voltage sag is contrasted and the attributes of a three-phase induction machine running in the ordinary condition. By using MATLAB/Simulink analyzed the performance of induction machine under-voltage swell and harmonics distortion.

articleTitle: Malware Analysis for Proactive Defence on Cyber Threat Vulnerabilities
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: In the current era of modernization, hackers are constantly improving themselves and discovering easy ways for creating malwares. Hackers generally use malwares to attack their targets and enable multiple forms of cyber-attacks. We propose to create a malicious software using the metasploit framework and analyze its behavior and the risk it poses. To achieve this we use meterpreter, which is an attack payload, that creates an environment for the hacker to explore the target's machine and execute code. The target machine is tested for threat analysis after successfully executing the code. The hacker will now be able to download files, take screenshots, live screen recording, grepping for passwords, escalate privileges, capture keystrokes, connect apps, download apps from the target, encrypt files for demanding ransom, and deny the services requested by the target. The proposed work executes a malware and performs the actions that a hacker can exploit a vulnerable device. This provides an insight of the current status of malware creation and comparing of different types of malwares.

articleTitle: A Unified Perspective on Modelling of Fractional Order-Sensorless MRAS Observer Based VSI Fed Induction Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: In recent years, there has been a growing exploitation of sensorless speed control or sway of Induction Motor drives across an extensive range of applications, from industrial to domestic electrical appliances. Sensorless Induction Motor drives offer numerous benefits such as reduced costs, increased reliability, simplified hardware, improved noise insusceptibility, and decreased maintenance needs. This article incorporates and integrate the active flux to analysis the fundamental frequency sensorless algorithm to examine the speed estimation of Induction Motors and additionally, it introduces a study of Fractional-Order controlled based Voltage Source Inverter (FO-VSI) fed Induction Motor model to improve closed-loop speed control's effectiveness in variable speed Induction Motor drives. A self-sensing algorithm employs Model Reference Adaptive Systems (MRAS) based on rotor-flux is used because of its advantages in variable speed drives like low speed operation, noise sensitivity, dynamic behavior, parameter sensitivity, and a good computational time as speed observer. Contrariwise, the Field-Oriented-Control (FOC) of the FO-VSI modeled Induction Motor improves speed tracking by minimizing control effort, especially when dealing with load disturbances. Finally, this article presents the results and characteristics of the Field-Oriented Control for the Induction Motor Drive with MRAS Speed Observer through use of MATLAB/Simulink numerical simulations. The findings indicate that FO-VSI Induction Motor drives have the potential to maintain lower speed operation even in the presence of load disturbances.

articleTitle: Optimization of Distribution System Reliability Using Dandelion Optimizer
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: This study proposes the Dandelion Optimizer (DO), a novel nature-inspired algorithm based on dandelion plant life cycles, for optimizing lightning protection system (LPS) placement in radial distribution networks with 81 buses. The objective is to minimize System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI) and Momentary Average Interruption Frequency Index (MAIFI). The DO offers a user-friendly approach to determining optimal solutions and excels in pinpointing optimal LPS deployment locations within distribution systems, concurrently fastening the calculation of SAIFI and MAIFI. Validation involves comprehensive numerical simulations, considering lightning flashover rate, distribution feeder attributes, and LPS configuration. Comparative analysis with Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) and Dragonfly Algorithm (DA) affirms DO's superior performance. Notably, DO showcases better capability in finding local optima and faster convergence than GWO and DA. Applying DO to optimise the optimal placements of LPSs yields a commendable 6.16% reduction in reliability indices, surpassing GWO and DA's 6.14% and 5.14% reductions. DO also exhibits heightened convergence speed over GWO and DA.

articleTitle: Detailed Analysis of Electric Vehicles and Solar-Powered Charging Stations
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Rising industrialization and worldwide economic expansion are driving up the cost of fuel and other commodities. The cost of using a private transport service has skyrocketed. The invention is the key to solving all these issues. Increasing the usage of renewable energy like solar electricity as an alternative to fossil fuels is one of the most workable options. Owning a commercially feasible electric car is everyone's dream, and it's getting closer and closer every day. These days, we can get an electric car for a reasonable sum. This is a chance to create a solar-powered station to charge electric cars. This research focuses on a solar-powered charging station, which is used to replenish electric vehicle (EV) batteries.

articleTitle: An Improved Differential Evolution for Offline Parameter Estimation in Lithium-Ion Batteries with Real-World Usage Data
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Offline parameter extraction for state-of-charge estimation (SoC) in a BMS setup for Li-ion cells (cell level and pack level) is realized using an improved differential evolution optimization algorithm. Battery modeling is performed using a 1-RC Thevenin's equivalent circuit model (ECM). Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) is used in conjunction with the proposed IDE algorithm to validate its efficiency at SoC estimation for cell-level Hybrid Pulse Power Characterization (HPPC) test and real-world driving test data. Compared to the standard HPPC method, recursive least squares estimation (RLSE), and the classical DE methods, the proposed method is capable of estimating the offline parameters accurately with lower RMSE for the EKF-based SoC estimation.

articleTitle: Grid Integration Improvement of the Wind Energy for a Hybrid Systems based FACTS
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: The main objective of this research is to study the performance of different models for hybrid systems to ameliorate grid-connection of wind power based on ESSs or FACTS controller. Different schemes and control techniques are studied, analysis and compared via modeling and simulation. In this study, a comparative studied among both control techniques for the hybrid systems has been achieved. In two configurations, an electrochemical power unit is inserted to DC-bus of the generator for a wind system and the model without batteries is applied as main case. Ultimately, the performance of a WF provided with constant-speed wind turbines inserted to the electrical grid through three various FACTS devices has been investigated. Finally, the comparative study of FACTS devices an adequate control of the voltage at the PCC to the utility grid of WF with decreased reactive power exchange if the series-connected system such as, SSSC is applied, while shunt-connected system such as, SVC and STATCOM provide an increased supply reactive power to the constant-speed wind generators. The main novelty and contribution of this article have been made to the scope of study where various control techniques for the hybrid systems encompass WECS & ESS have been modeled, analyzed and compared at different cases. These techniques have been aimed to dominate of DFIG converters used in the wind generators. These studies comprised evaluation under fluctuating wind, variable demand and simulation at different grid fault. Control systems for STATCOM, SVC and SSSC have been depicted to ameliorate the grid-connection of a WF based on SCIGs. The dynamic response of these FACTS has been studied, analysis and compared through simulation. Simulation results present the voltage stability of the WF is improved by the SSSC device whereas STATCOM & SVC give additional reactive power.

articleTitle: Numerical Modelling of Evacuated Tube Collector and Evaluation of Integrating Thermal Storage Materials
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: The paper presents the numerical modelling of an evacuated tube collector system (ETC) and evaluation of adding thermal storage material. The aim is to assess the effect, performance, and operating hours of the ETC system. The chosen thermal storage material are Acetamide, Magnesium nitrate hexahydrate, and Desert sand. Both Acetamide and Magnesium nitrate hexahydrate are examples of phase change materials (PCM). Melting temperature of Acetamide is 80°C while Magnesium nitrate hexahydrate is 89°C. Proposed system is suitable for domestic, and commercial purposes. Hence, ETC modules can produce high temperatures by adding more collector tubes and optimizing the mass flow rate. Mass flowrates can also affect heat energy supplied to the ETC system and time duration. Numerical results obtained indicate that an ETC system integrated with thermal storage material can prolong and maintain the temperature of hot water in the system.

articleTitle: Detecting and Fixing SQL Injection and Cross-Site Scripting Vulnerabilities in Web Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: More people have access to the internet than ever before. This has prompted many organizations to develop web-based applications that users can use online to interact with the organization. Poorly written code for web applications, especially SQL queries can be exploited to gain unauthorized access to sensitive data and web servers. It is not possible to manually scroll through the codebase to detect parts of code that would make the application vulnerable to attacks. Thus, machine learning and natural language processing-based solutions would help detect such queries either based on their patterns or signatures or through training via previous attack datasets. This paper aims to propose a novel methodology to detect SQL injection vulnerable queries and Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks using pattern matching and NLP techniques and rewrite or in other words correct the vulnerable parts of code to prevent such attacks. Overall, this paper is used to identify vulnerable parts of code in a given client-side PHP web application, detect if the vulnerability belongs to a particular attack type and finally correct the vulnerable section of the code by providing recommendations based on standard prevention techniques for the corresponding attacks.

articleTitle: Image Data Hiding Scheme Using Adversarial Embedding
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Data and information are increasingly at risk due to developments in science and technology. Several strategies for hiding information have been proposed to deal with these threats. Hiding information in a picture is the most commonly used method since it is difficult for an outsider to detect hidden information. Data coverage can be improved by using different deep learning and artificial intelligence techniques. This paper proposes a deep learning based framework steganography embedding-extraction architecture for embedding pictures as payloads. To achieve this, we have made some important contributions: (i) the general encoder-coder architecture, which encodes and decodes all sequences of pixels, is proposed;(ii) we are introducing a loss function that ensures the training of embedded extraction networks; (iii) on a range of freely available datasets, we will be doing a thorough analysis of the proposal for architecture; and (iv) to enhance security and quality of image, we are introducing a new adversary network for the detection of stego images. Indicate the high levels of PSNR and SSIM with cutting-edge payload capacities.

articleTitle: Power Transmission Line Inspection Using Unmanned Aerial Vehicle - A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: In recent years unmanned aerial vehicles are used in various inspection applications like construction operations, turbine, sewage water treatment, wind mill, power lines etc. In this study the need of UAVs in power transmission line is taken into account because even now in many countries manual labour is used for the inspection. Also the power lines need a regular maintenance in order to transmit required power supply. The aim of this work is to present a review on various artificial techniques that are used to collect the various data from the power transmission lines. Further the basic needs of hardware requirements for the UAV design are discussed in detail. Based on the study, the challenges and need of UAV are summarized in the concluding remarks.

articleTitle: Integration of Convolutional Neural Network and Support Vector Regression for Electricity Price Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Accurate electricity price forecasting (EPF) plays a crucial role in bid strategies and risk reduction for market participants in the competitive electricity market. However, forecasting of electricity prices accurately is a highly demanding task due to the intricate nonlinearity present in the price dynamics. This paper introduces a combination of deep learning (DL) technique with machine learning (ML) model to forecast electricity prices in the Australian energy market operator (AEMO) for hourly price prediction utilizing load and renewable energy supply data from five major economical states New South Wales (NSW), Queensland (QLD), South Australia (SA), Tasmania (TAS) and Victoria (VIC). The proposed work integrates the convolutional neural network (CNN) and support vector regression (SVR) to identify short-term local dependency patterns among variables and uncover long-term correlations for time series patterns and forecast the hourly ahead price. The suggested model (CNN-SVR) is contrasted to various models such as CNN-LSTM, BiLSTM, SVR, and their performance is evaluated using various metrics, including mean absolute error (MAE), mean square error (MSE), and root mean square error (RMSE).

articleTitle: Design of Printable Microstrip Patch Antenna on Flexible Substrate for Medical Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: The microstrip patch antenna design has been a research topic for biomedical applications. Thus, the systems operate at a few gigahertz frequencies, resulting in a suboptimal resolution, and jeopardizing image superiority. Therefore, quality resolutions could be achieved using a millimeter wave (mm-wave) with a large operational Bandwidth frequency range. This article proposed a 28 GHz printable rectangular microstrip patch antenna, designed using a flexible polyamide substrate in CST studio software with a compact size of (5 × 5mm2). The effect of substrate thickness and slot widths of radiating element on frequency response was analyzed to achieve better Bandwidth at minimum return loss. A gain of 3.04 dBi and a Bandwidth of 8.65 GHz resonated from 21.51 GHz – 30.16 GHz, with an average radiation efficiency of 82%, return loss of 43.44 dB, and voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) of 1.014 was achieved. The antenna achieved a bidirectional pattern to be placed in either a back or front position and polymer-based materials used are one option for reducing power consumption. The research outcome suggests that the use of an mm-wave antenna with an appropriate substrate thickness of (0.125 mm) makes it suitable for the proposed applications.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Road Traffic Sign Recognition System Based on CNN and Yolo v5
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Exemplary drivers prioritize adherence to traffic rules, and implementing traffic sign detection technology effectively supports such behavior, enhancing road safety for all road users. This paper brings a comparative analysis of road traffic sign recognition systems based on Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and You Only Look Once version 5 (Yolo v5) on the German Traffic Sign Recognition Benchmark (GTSRB) dataset. The proposed recognition system consists of four stages: 1) dataset annotation; 2) data pre-processing to lower noise; 3) sign detection and classification; 4) performance analysis. The developed models can detect and recognize forty-three classes of traffic signs covering all existing traffic signs under varying light and noise conditions as available in the dataset. Libraries and tools like Keras, TensorFlow, SKlearn, OpenCV2, Google Colab, etc., have been used to pre-process the data in Python. The processed images will serve as the CNN and Yolo v5 training datasets. According to experimental findings, the CNN model outperforms the YOLO v5 model in successfully identifying the majority of traffic signals with a precision of 96.231%. The proposed system would be helpful for the development of autonomous vehicles and provide effective driving assistance messages.

articleTitle: ML and DL-based Segmentation and Classification of Different Types of Venous Thrombosis
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Venous thrombosis (VT) can happen for no obvious cause, but it is generally formed in deep veins in our body due to injury or too sluggish blood flow. It is a devastating condition with severe morbidity and fatality rates. This model involves a novel, impressive pre-processing technique that could prove to be an enhancement tool for different types of thrombus by reducing non-uniform revelation while preserving its edges. Usually, algorithms used for classification estimation fail to include constraints like sharp edges, spatial smoothness, orientation, intensity and lesion variation features while preserving their naturalness, which is essential in defining the state of the affected anatomical region. Deep learning (DL) based VGGNet-19 is used to classify VT, which is often underdiagnosed and preventable. Performance analysis is conducted and outcomes are compared to existing techniques to prove effectiveness.

articleTitle: Electrothermal Modelling of Squirrel Cage Induction Machine with Winding Fault Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Electrothermal analysis has great potential as an approach for monitoring the health of electric machines. The thermal analysis gives precise information for early fault detection. An insulation deterioration in machine winding creates a short circuit which leads to an inter-turn fault and, if not discovered, phase-phase fault or phase-ground fault may occur. To understand the electrical and thermal behaviour of machines under various stages of fault conditions, electrothermal modelling is mandatory. This paper develops the electrothermal model of a 2.2 kW squirrel cage induction machine with various winding faults in the Matlab/Simulink platform. Based on simulation findings the phase currents and short circuit loop current spikes under different fault scenarios and load conditions were derived. To evaluate the impact of faults on machine behaviour, variations in electrical and thermal characteristics under healthy and faulty systems were analyzed. The symmetrical and asymmetrical winding faults including single-phase faults, two-phase faults and three-phase faults were created with 2% and 6% severity.

articleTitle: Optimal Placement and Sizing of Single DG to Minimize Energy Loss and Optimizing Voltage Profile Based on Optimized Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Distributed energy represents an economical and reliable source of electricity for consumers. They are attached immediately to distribution unit at points of contact with consumers. The enforcements of distributed energy sources provide numerous refinements to distribution system performance like improving the energy efficiency, voltage profile, contribute to reduce grid failures and improve reliability of the grid. In this article, three techniques were suggested to achieve optimal size & position of distributed power generators and fixed capacitors into radial systems. These methods are Moth-Flame (MFO), Multi-Verse (MVO), and Whale optimization (WOA) algorithms. The main target of each of these methods is to optimize its size and placement of the distributed resources in distribution units with a purpose ameliorate grid performance by reducing energy loss, enhance the stability of voltages and to compare among the above-mentioned algorithms on the basis of true power losses, voltage profile amelioration and convergence characteristics.

articleTitle: Hardware Implementation of Anaerobic Biogas Digester for Household and Community Purposes
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: 1.3 billion tons of food that get thrown out every year is a huge problem, not only does it create methane and carbon dioxide, which contribute to climate change, but it also takes up valuable space in landfills. There is a solution that is waste to energy.It is a process where food waste is used to create energy, this can be done through combustion, anaerobic digestion, or other means.N ot only does this reduce the amount of food waste that goes to landfills, but it also provides a renewable energy source. Proposed system is a anaerobic digestor that is temperature controlled, stirring, with solar panels and battery backup. Anaerobic digestion is a sustainable method for recovering biofuel from organic waste materials such as animal manure or plant material discarded after harvest, the byproduct generated during this process is effluent and it can act as a fertilizer for plants, and soil amendment purposes.

articleTitle: Rainfall Presage Forecast Using Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Rainfall prediction is vital for various applications such as agriculture, flood control, and water resource management. Accurate rainfall prediction can help farmers to make decisions about irrigation and crop selection. It can also help authorities to take necessary measures to prevent or mitigate the impact of floods. In the proposed study, multiple algorithms are examined and compared in terms of how accurately they predict rainfall. The accuracy of rainfall forecasts may be increased by using machine learning algorithms, which have shown considerable promise in predicting rainfall patterns. The authors solely used the AUC score and categorial standards to analyze six ML algorithms. Based on their accuracy score, AUC, precision, recall, and f1 score, authors compared algorithms including Random Forest, K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN), Logistic Regression, Cat Boost, Naive Bayes, and Gradient Boost. Since they provide a useful solution for categorization and prediction of the amount of rainfall as well as precise rate prediction, the applied algorithms are supervised learning algorithms.

articleTitle: Supply Chain Management Using Blockchain and IoT in Pharmaceutical Industries
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: The pharmaceutical industry is very important for the functioning of modern society with its huge impact on the economy. The pharmaceutical industry has contributed to increasing life expectancy, improving patient conditions, and providing the necessary medicines and treatments to millions of people around the world. The blockchain and IoT based pharmaceutical supply chain project is an initiative that aims to improve the existing pharmaceutical supply chain models by using cutting-edge technologies such as IoT and blockchain. The system developed will collect and monitor real-time data on pharmaceutical products such as temperature and humidity to ensure the condition of products. To enhance the transparency and security of the pharmaceutical supply chain blockchain which is an immutable and decentralized ledger-based system in combination with IoT to ensure the integrity of the data gathered using IoT devices such as sensors are used. Smart contracts are used to automate supply chain processes. The project faces constraints such as cost, integration with current systems, trade-offs between security and performance, decentralization, and scalability. By taking constraints and other factors into account, we aim to deliver a project that will improve supply chain outcomes.

articleTitle: Driver Stress and Workload Based Experience Analysis to Compute the Effects of Designing and Calibrating In-Car Navigation System
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: The design of in-car navigation systems is a critical factor in determining driver stress levels and workload. This study seeks to collect information on drivers' experiences with in-car navigation systems, specifically their stress and workload levels. By analyzing the data collected, researchers can identify design features that contribute to both positive and negative user experiences, informing future navigation system design and development. Furthermore, results of this study could be used for improving existing systems' user experiences (UX), relieving driver stress, and encouraging safer driving practices on the road. The increasing demand for in-car navigation systems has led to the proliferation of these devices in vehicles. While these devices provide useful information for drivers, they can also contribute to driver stress and workload. The complexity of these systems, along with their frequent use during driving, can cause distraction and increase mental workload, which can ultimately lead to accidents. Based on the findings, in-car navigation system accuracy rates were highest for individuals within the age range 25 – 45 and range 18 – 24 with accuracy rates at 89.54095 respectively, while its accuracy rate for 46 – 68 individuals ranged between 64.3802-63.50802. These findings hold significant ramifications for the design and development of in-car navigation systems, particularly with respect to relieving driver stress and workload associated with their usage.

articleTitle: Marker-Based AR Enabled Online Electronics Purchasing Web Application
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: A marker-based augmented reality (AR) enabled online electronics purchasing web application is presented in this paper to provide users with an intuitive and interactive shopping experience. The proposed system allows users to see how the electronics product will look in real life by scanning markers on them with the camera of a mobile device and overlaying 3D virtual models of the products on the screen. The application gives clients detailed information about the items, including specifications, reviews, and pricing, and allows them to add the items to their cart and purchase them directly from the web application. By providing users with a more realistic view of the products they are interested in and reducing the likelihood of dissatisfaction due to erroneous expectations, the proposed system aims to enhance the experience of online shopping. A user study was used to assess the effectiveness of the proposed system. It found that people preferred the AR-enabled shopping experience to the traditional online shopping experience.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Smart Nebulizer Using IoT in the Treatment of Asthma Patients
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Asthma and other respiratory diseases impose a significant global burden, affecting millions of individuals and placing substantial strain on health care systems. The domain of healthcare has witnessed transformative advancements through the integration of Internet of Things (IoT) technology, fostering the emergence of patient-centric solutions. Respiratory ailments pose significant challenges to patients, necessitating precise management and monitoring. Existing conventional inhalers often lack automation, real time monitoring, data driven insights and overall polish that leads to suboptimal treatment, but in no way, it could match with other peripherals which have advanced quite significantly over the years. Our proposed solution presents an IoT-based smart inhaler that seamlessly captures inhalation data, securely transmits it to the cloud, and employs data analytics to offer personalized recommendations. One of the key innovations of our project is the integration of real-time monitoring and feedback. By equipping the Nebulizer device with sensors and communication modules, we empower users with instant insights into their Nebulizer usage patterns. Comparison reveals that while conventional inhalers offer basic functionality, they lack the data-driven insights and remote monitoring capabilities of the IoT smart nebulizer. Future enhancements can encompass AI-driven predictive analytics, enabling early detection of exacerbations, and incorporation of wearable respiratory sensors for a comprehensive health overview.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Smart Driver Monitoring System With Emergency Response Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Sleep deprivation, driver fatigue and lack of attentiveness while driving are among the causes of fatal road accidents. This paper proposed a way to tackle the issues mentioned with the assistance of the Internet-of-Things that can detect driver drowsiness and monitor the driver's heart rate. The driver will be continuously monitored through a camera embedded with the proposed system where the driver's facial expression data can be obtained, which will be used to determine if the driver is yawning. With the aid of external stimuli such as alarms and vibrations, an alert will be generated if the driver is in a drowsy state. An emergency response mechanism is incorporated into the system where an alert message will be sent to the driver's next of kin. A mobile application is also being developed for monitoring the pulse rate. The proposed system is portable and provides a potential solution to improve the safety of drivers on the road and prevent road accidents.

articleTitle: Forest Fire Classification of Montesinho Park Using Artificial Neural Network and Fuzzy Logic
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Wildfires, which start spontaneously and are uncontrollable, as well as spontaneous fires that start in rural areas and have an impact on the vegetation, have historically been frequent natural occurrences. Wildfires are particularly common in forested areas, meadows, scrublands, and comparable habitats. These terrible occurrences can take place anywhere and are not limited to locations, environments, or continents. Fuzzy algorithms and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) are sophisticated approaches that have been developed to effectively classify wildfires. The ANN model and fuzzy algorithm play a key role in maximising the results of the classification of wildfires. The algorithm can handle ambiguous or imprecise data related to wildfires by using fuzzy logic, resulting in more reliable and precise predictions. This aids in developing a better understanding of wildfire behaviour and putting in place useful preventative measures. The neural networks can be effectively trained to classify wildfires according to their severity, spread, and potential effects by using the Feed Forward Back propagation (FFB) algorithm. The optimised results from this classification process offer important insights for policymakers, emergency response teams, and forest management authorities. Appropriate strategies can be developed to lessen wildfires' destructive effects and safeguard both human lives and ecosystems by understanding their nature and behaviour.A thorough and effective method of classifying wildfires is provided by the combination of the FFB propagation algorithm with the ANN and fuzzy algorithms. Utilising these cutting-edge methods, we can learn important things about how wildfires behave, allowing for more efficient preparation, response, and mitigation efforts.

articleTitle: Compressor Fault Diagnosis Employing Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Compressors are a potent and crucial component in the industry as they make the work environment fresh, secure, and convenient. Heavy use of this equipment tends to make them faulty. Effective fault identification is a major need for the incessant use of compressors in the industry. Various compressor faults like Bearing faults, Flywheel faults, NRV faults, and LOV faults are considered in the work. Healthy and faulty samples (1024 samples) are taken and preprocessed using Wavelet Transform, such as Daubechies4 and Daubechies10. Statistical measures, namely Error, Skewness, Standard Deviation, Variance, and Kurtosis were computed. Machine learning methods namely KNN, SVM, and Random forest were applied to the statistical measures. A comparison of the three machine learning-based methods was carried out and three other performance metrics such as Precision, Recall, and F1 score have been evaluated. It was proved that KNN had a maximum accuracy (85%) over the other methods. An attempt to improve the accuracy is being carried out by increasing the number of samples and by applying specific preprocessing techniques.

articleTitle: A Resilience-Oriented Network Restoration Model for a Flood-Hit Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: High-impact low-probability (HILP) events such as earthquakes, snowstorms, and flooding severely damage power system infrastructure that results in longer and widespread power outages. These extended electricity cuts adversely affect economic activities and cause significant monetary loss. Therefore, a rapid network restoration strategy following a natural disaster is of utmost importance. In this respect, a resilient network restoration model is presented to minimize interruption costs while considering the damage to the substation, the traveling time of repair crews, and repair time. The percentage damage of an inundated substation is determined by an existing flood damage model and repair time is estimated through regression analysis. The Monte Carlo technique is then used to evaluate the expected interruption cost. Finally, the routing of repair crews is optimized by employing Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm to minimize customer interruption costs. The proposed methodology is tested on a modified IEEE 33-bus test system.

articleTitle: Minimising Energy Consumption Cost Using Ant Colony Optimization with Power Quality Considerations Under HEMS Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Today's technology intends to simplify daily activities, leading to increased energy demands. The consumption of electrical energy is rising swiftly as a result of the rapid advancements in technology. Over 80% of domestic electrical energy consumption is attributed to consumer negligence. The cost and demand of electrical energy consumption by consumers will have significant implications on the power system. The inclusion of power quality issues is necessary when accounting for the aforementioned constraints. The importance of a Home Energy Management System (HEMS) is emphasised in addressing this issue. This paper explores optimisation strategies for enhancing the efficiency of the Home Energy Management System (HEMS) under various conditions. The objective of this work is to utilise ant colony optimisation and implement a Load Scheduling Algorithm based on it. The Constraints will be considered before scheduling the residential loads. This study proposes a fixed energy consumption cost for the entire day by scheduling required loads at various intervals. The present work discusses the Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) algorithm, categorised as a lower complexity evolutionary algorithm for cost consumption estimation and comparison of various scheduling and non-scheduling loads considering the impact of harmonics.

articleTitle: AI Based Cloud Failure Detection and Prevention Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: It is crucial to anticipate and avoid cloud breakdowns to guarantee the availability and dependability of cloud services. Machine learning algorithms have shown promise in forecasting and preventing cloud failures by analyzing large datasets of cloud usage traces to identify potential failure points. This paper presents an algorithm incorporating different Machine Learning and Deep Learning models for cloud failure prediction and prevention based on analyzing the Google cluster usage traces dataset. The proposed algorithm, the AI-based Cloud Failure Prevention Algorithm (ACFP), utilizes various features to predict potential failure points. The proposed algorithm used various AI models, the prominent ones are Cat Boost (accuracy, F1 score, Precision, Specificity: 100%), LGB (accuracy, F1 score, Precision, Specificity: 100%), Gradient Boost (accuracy, F1 score, Precision, Specificity: 100%), Random Forest (accuracy, F1 score, Precision, Specificity: 100%), etc. for the precise detection of cloud task failure.After that the ACFP selects one ML/DL model with best failure prediction efficiency and use some parameters like: “resource_utilization”, “event_type”, and “scheduler” to generate some suggestion based values for the cloud so that the cloud implements that suggestion to prevent cloud failure. The experimental results show how well the algorithm predicts and averts cloud breakdowns, highlighting its potential to raise the reliability and availability of cloud services. The comparison of the failure rate of the cloud by predicting job failures with and without the ACFP is 2.67% and 22.76%, respectively. This algorithm can raise the quality of cloud services and reduce the risks of cloud failures.

articleTitle: Agronomic Soil Testing Miniature with WSN
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Agriculture is considered to be the main resource for the growth of a country. As the population grows drastically, agriculture is a field that needs to be concentrated to feed the entire community. To meet the entire demand, farmers are handling many short-cut techniques to harvest crops within a shorter period. Crop health is not well understood by experimenting with many fast-growing techniques; ultimately, the consumer who is consuming the crop is also affected. To mitigate these issues, which carefully looks at the healthy yield that fits into the proper time frame, precision agricultural technology comes into play. A collective miniature prototype model of all agronomic sensors such as environmental temperature and humidity sensor, soil moisture sensor, rainfall detecting sensor, pH sensor, and nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium detecting sensors are integrated. The module helps the farmer to analyze the particular field that is sufficient to grow healthy crops. The developed model is tested for its functionality in a farm and analyzed. The crop health is being compared with the crop being tested with the developed model and without the model. From the real-time test analysis, the developed model produced effective growth with proper monitoring. It also reduces the manual time consumption of a farmer for incorporating the entire process with the developed model. Simultaneously, it alerts the farmer depending upon the monitored status through the Wi-Fi embedded with the module.

articleTitle: Partial Discharge Analysis of Bio Degradable Nano Filled Oil Under Different Electrode Geometry
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Abundant insulation between different active parts of the transformer is mandatory for its prudent operation. Nano filled bio degradable oil is used as an insulating medium as an alternative for mineral oil in a transformer. Electrical discharges known as partial discharges (PDs) take place in the transformers' insulating system. Transformer insulation system stagnation is caused by the PDs phenomenon. To prevent the transformer from completely breaking down, it is vital to calculate and detect the PD at a primary stage. The PDIV and PD characteristic of Nano-filled biodegradable oil were discussed, and tests were carried out using electrode configurations with needle plane and rod plane. With the oil in the test cell, PDIV and PD activities of Nano filled biodegradable oil were compared and studied. The impact of oil condition on PDIV and PD features was taken into account. The maximum electric field stress is shown by changes in electrode arrangement, and conversely, the measured PDIV value is shown to be the lowest.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Design, Control Interlocking Logic, and Network Analysis in 132 kV Substations
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: The increasing demand for electricity, driven by economic growth and population expansion, necessitates the enhancement of electrical systems, particularly in the design of substations and other power system components. In a modern power system comprising power generation plants, transmission networks, diverse loads, and advanced substations equipped with automation and communication technologies, substations play a pivotal role alongside generators and transmission lines. This work undertakes a comparative analysis of 132 kV substations, focusing on their design and control interlocking logic. The design disparities are examined by assessing Gas Insulated Substations (GIS) and Air Insulated Substations (AIS) characteristics, while control interlocking logic differences are explored concerning the conditions for operating Circuit Breakers (CB), isolators, and earth switches. Moreover, network analysis is conducted encompassing load flow analysis and fault analysis.

articleTitle: Diagnosis of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome Using Machine Learning Models: A Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) is a serious health problem affecting a significant percentage of female population worldwide during their reproductive years and adolescence. Besides being one of the leading causes of female infertility, PCOS also carries risks of long-term health issues such as diabetes, high blood pressure, and cardiovascular disease. While PCOS is not curable, proper treatment can alleviate some symptoms. Hence, timely diagnosis is crucial for effective treatment. PCOS diagnosis is challenging due to varying symptoms among affected women. Recently, promising progress in medical diagnosis has been made using machine learning techniques. This paper presents a comparative analysis of the performance of single classifier-based machine learning models and ensemble machine learning models in diagnosing PCOS using benchmark Kaggle PCOS dataset. 10-fold cross-validation has been used to assess the performance of the models. From the experimental results it is observed that among the thirteen different machine learning models considered for this study, the Random Forest classifier has achieved the best performance with an accuracy and F1-score of 90.1% and 83.6% respectively.

articleTitle: A Modular Industrial IoT Scheme to Monitor and Control Distribution in a Substation Model
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: IoT - based remote monitoring and controlling of the substation is proposed in this work. It is done by using a Flexy-205 IoT Gateway and remote access router. The substation automation plant model has different model divisions such as City, Urban, Rural 1, and Rural 2, which have circuit breakers and lights. This model is controlled with the help of Siemens S7-300 programmable logic controller. A ladder logic program has developed in Simatic Manager software. The Flexy-205 is an advanced internet data gateway that allows machine builders to access and collect data remotely for evaluation and analytical maintenance. The remote access and data collection from the substation plant using S7-300 PLC with Flexy-205 is done by using Ebuddy and ECatcher software. The Graphical User Interface for substation remote access is created using viewON software. The proposed method is successfully tested on the substation remotely.

articleTitle: Intelligent Wireless Charging Station for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: The normal vehicles which uses fossil fuels will emit more harm full gases and damage the environment. The consequences of the environment like acid rains, global warming and greenhouse effect. For this the electric vehicles became a solution for it. The response of EVs is very acceptable and people are interested to use the EVs. The increasing price of fuels day to day its very harder to maintain the vehicle. Whereas EVs are easier and cheaper to maintain. These vehicles are run by electricity. By using EVs we will reduce noise pollution, air pollution and by using natural power as source we can save electricity also. The conventional method of charging the vehicle with a physical connection makes some disadvantageous like chance of sparks, the wire will get damaged using several years, and connection problems to avoid this we came up with wireless charging. Here, we are using “Inductive Coupling” method to charge the vehicle wirelessly. Our smart charging station is built with a unique idea, that is to use Hybrid energy. When a car enters into station the vehicle will recognized and a welcome message sent and he can check where the parking slot is available. If any slot is available the driver can notice by seeing display in car. Once the vehicle enters into hotspot it will automatically charge, there is no need for the customer to step out of the car. The user can get entertained by the things provided in dash board like games, music, etc., When the battery gets fully charged the battery gets auto cut off to save the battery life. The other services are also provided in station like cleaning the car, water washing, and other mechanic services required for a vehicle. By using all these things, the user can pay his bill through by using smart card where with just a single click he can pay the amount. The other services needed for an electric vehicle will be provided in station. This will create an employment opportunity for the people and increases automation. Here, we are designing an algorithm and block chain concept to keep the data secure and monitoring the station and cyber activites.

articleTitle: Designing Control for Markovian Switching Neural Network with Stochastic Perturbation
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: The main objective of the present study is to investigate and analyse the dynamic characteristics of neural networks (NNs) that are modeled as differential equations. There are various inevitable factors like time delays and external disturbances which may affect the network transmission. Besides the idea is to explore the stability properties of the NNs model that incorporates time-varying delays and stochastic disturbances. The sampled-data control scheme is proposed in this study due to its ability to handle the neuronal system with disturbances. The sampled-data control scheme is proposed in this study due to its ability to handle the neuronal system with stochastic disturbances. Theoretically, the synchronization problem with the objective of guaranteeing the global asymptotic stability of the error model arises from the drive (uncontrolled) and response (controlled) systems. In this regard, a two-sided looped Lyapunov Krasovskii Functional (LKF) candidate is considered. The sufficient stability conditions are derived in terms of solvable linear matrix inequalities(LMIs). The efficiency of the proposed model is evaluated through the numerical simulations of two neural models.

articleTitle: User Impersonation Detection and Authentication Using Image Based OTP
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: In this age of the internet and technology, it is very important to be vigilant with one's devices and have safe and secure passwords to avoid several types of crimes. In this paper, we concentrate on two types of attacks: user impersonation and shoulder surfing. User impersonation is the act where one person pretends to be you or someone else to create confusion or obtain information that is private to you. To prevent this, we discuss a method to classify a person as authorised or unauthorised, utilising data from the user's mobile device's accelerometer and gyroscope sensors [1]. One of the simplest methods scammers use to acquire your personal information is by shoulder surfing, which may be as easy as simply looking over your shoulder. It is extremely common and hard to prevent in crowded areas. We proposed a method of authentication that uses OTPs and graphical password techniques and would prove effective against shoulder surfing attacks.

articleTitle: Modeling, Design, and Implementation of Electric Tri-Wheeler
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Transportation sector is the second largest in utilization of fossil fuels. The impact of fossil fuel depletion and emissions from Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) vehicles on the environment that contributes to the climate changes and global warming signifies the need for alternative solutions to transportation means such as electric vehicles. Differently abled people are mostly using modified two wheelers (4 wheeled scooters) to assist their mobility needs. Such vehicles have several disadvantages and are of great discomfort to the rider. Keeping in mind the necessities of differently abled people, a custom designed electric tri-wheeler is proposed. This paper gives an insight into modeling and design of the electric vehicle with step-by-step procedure. The design procedure is explained in detail with necessary equations. The structure design is performed using SolidWorks and the strength of the designed structure is analyzed with Finite Element Analysis (FEA). The deformation test is carried out and the torsional deformation test is conducted in ANSYS R15.0. The proposed electric tri-wheeler is built and tested. The vehicle performance is found very satisfactory. The overall operating cost of the vehicle is lower than that of the conventional modified twowheeler and the vehicle is more sustainable with zero emission.

articleTitle: Sweep Spot: Empowering Communities for Sustainable Waste Management in Urban Areas
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Rapid urbanization has led to a surge in garbage production, causing severe environmental and public health concerns. A trash management system has been designed using mobile technologies and geolocation services to address this problem. Users can take, and post automatically geotagged photos of trash. The system incorporates an API to offer information on the closest municipality in charge of waste management. Based on user feedback, analysis and action are made more accessible by a backend database. An algorithm has been put in place to assess how close the user's position is to the nearest municipality. By streamlining garbage reporting and promoting cleaner, more sustainable urban environments, the system hopes to improve interaction with local government agencies.

articleTitle: Student Placement Prediction Using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: The student placement prediction plays a crucial role in modern educational institutions and the job market. To make informed decisions with machine learning algorithms, accurate placement prediction has become achievable. This model focuses on the application of machine learning algorithms for placement prediction, analyzing their effectiveness, and comparing their performance. Educational institutions that facilitate this process can identify areas of improvement in their curriculum and career counseling services, leading to better student outcomes and satisfaction. To save time and resources for companies, it helps optimize their hiring process. This model also focuses on the implementation of machine learning algorithms that can accurately predict whether a student will be placed or not, based on a set of input features such as academic scores, internship experience, activities, and more. This model supports other machine learning algorithms. It provides valuable insights into student employability factors and contributes to fostering a better future for both students and the job market. However, updating the model with fresh data and refinement ensures its accuracy and relevance in an ever-changing job landscape.

articleTitle: Non-isolated Bidirectional DC-DC Converter for BLDC Motor in Electric Vehicle Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: This paper proposes a Bidirectional DC-DC converter (BDC) that interfaces a battery pack and motor load for Electric Vehicle (EV) applications. The proposed converter is capable of operating in two distinct modes i.e. (i) Battery charging mode with boost operation and (ii) Battery discharging mode with Buck operation, and with the features of bidirectional power flow control.
